title: $\mathrm{Cons}(X,\Lambda)$ is essentially small
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, and let $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ be defined
in a fixed universe. Then the isomorphism classes of objects of $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ form a set.
Here $\ell$ is a prime, $E$ is a finite subextension of a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and the coefficient rings are the condensed rings of [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back as $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. In particular these are not the discrete constant coefficient sheaves. The full category $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ is that of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Sets and small site skeletons are taken in the larger universe $\mathcal V$ of [def-weil-size-convention], with the schemes and coefficient data in its fixed smaller bound $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$.

proof.text: Work directly with internal coefficient modules, without changing the actual condensed coefficient ring. A finitely presented module is a cokernel of a map between two finite free modules [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Encode it by two natural numbers and the morphism in the locally small Hom set. The family of these cokernels is small in the larger universe [def-weil-size-convention], and every finitely presented module is isomorphic to one of them. This is the private Lean lemma finitelyPresentedSmall.

Use the following elementary smallness argument, implemented as boundedByMonos and smallFromRestrictions. In a locally small well-powered category, objects admitting a monomorphism into a small family of objects are essentially small: take the union of the essential images of their MonoOver categories. Given a small family of left adjoints L_i with right adjoints R_i and essentially small properties P_i, select small representative properties Q_i. For a tuple of representatives Y_i, form H = product_i R_i Y_i. The adjunction transposes of chosen isomorphisms L_i M ≅ Y_i give t:M→H. The composite of L_i(t), the image of the product projection and the counit equals that isomorphism, so L_i(t) is monic. If the L_i jointly reflect monomorphisms, t is monic. Module categories have the required products and well-poweredness by [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] and Mathlib IsGrothendieckAbelian.hasLimits/wellPowered.

For a pro-etale cover, coefficient-module restrictions jointly reflect isomorphisms: pass through the faithful forgetful functor using profinitePointModuleForgetPullbackIso from [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], then use the existing upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction and isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction for abelian sheaves. These are the canonical localization computation for [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] on the site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. They jointly reflect monomorphisms as well: apply restriction to the kernel of a map; exact pullback makes its restrictions zero, and reflection of the kernel-to-zero isomorphism gives zero kernel. This is coverReflectsIso/coverReflectsMono. The coefficient-module adjunctions and exact pullbacks are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback].

Fix a cover U. The possible local restrictions are the functorial images of the finitely presented point-module property under upperStarFromPoint(U_i).mapMod. Images of essentially small properties are essentially small (Mathlib ObjectProperty.Small). Apply step 2 to the cover restrictions and step 3. Taking the small union over Scheme.Cover.{u} gives essential smallness of HasFiniteConstantLocalModel from [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. No choice of a finite basis and no explicit transition matrices are needed. Covers need not be finite. This is constantLocalModelsSmall.

For a finite stratification S, restrictions to its actual immersions jointly reflect monomorphisms. A map g with g f = 0 becomes zero on each stratum when every restriction of f is monic. Transfer this vanishing through profinitePointModuleForgetPullbackIso [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. The proved private abDetectMaps in the module of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-abelian-closed-support] detects zero abelian-sheaf maps for any finite jointly surjective family of quasi-compact scheme maps. Its hypotheses hold: the stratum images cover X, and on the Noetherian underlying space every immersed stratum has a Noetherian domain, hence its immersion is quasi-compact. Faithfulness of forgetting module actions gives g=0, so f is monic. This directly uses joint detection without converting Scheme.Stratification to another interface.

Apply step 2 over the finite set of strata with the essentially small local-model properties of step 4 and the joint mono detection of step 5. Then take the small union over Scheme.Stratification X. This proves that IsFiniteConstantStratified [sk-def-sfb-constructible] is essentially small; it is stratifiedModelsSmall. All indexing types lie in the universe fixed by [def-weil-size-convention].

Local Noetherianity gives quasi-separatedness [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; quasi-compactness is assumed. Thus the qcqs branch of IsConstantModelConstructible [sk-def-sfb-constructible] equals IsFiniteConstantStratified. Apply the Mathlib ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall instance for a full subcategory. Empty covers, the empty stratification and scheme, and rank-zero presentations satisfy the same argument. All lemmas before the final specialization allow an arbitrary commutative condensed ring, so the admissible coefficient cases follow without using field structure.

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs, small local models and gluing data; local models bounded by finite presentations and gluing by subobjects of products of right-adjoint images. Implemented from Mathlib ObjectProperty.Small, Subobject.WellPowered, and the existing abelian cover/stratum detection lemmas.
